root_cause_label: Failed to implement arithmetic coder matching decompressor format
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent recognized the decompressor uses adaptive arithmetic coding but lacked the knowledge to implement a matching range encoder, instead writing multiple naive bit-packing approaches that all produce incompatible bitstreams, and ultimately submitted an incompatible gzip file while explicitly acknowledging it would not work.
t_err_evidence: cat > comp.c - compressor outputs raw bits and 4-byte header, not arithmetic range-coded format decomp expects
t_commit_evidence: After writing the naive bit-packing compressor at step 6, every subsequent attempt (correct_comp.c at step 25, golomb_comp.c at step 29, final_comp.c at step 21) follows the same fundamental wrong paradigm of emitting raw bits instead of implementing the required range encoder with gc()-1 tokens; the agent never recovers from this structural design error.
t_surface_evidence: Segmentation fault (core dumped) when piping custom-compressed output through ./decomp
trigger_explanation: The agent correctly identified at step 2 that decomp.c implements adaptive arithmetic coding with context-based range decoding (radix=255, gc()-1 tokens, ctx*=99 context scaling), but lacked the domain knowledge to implement a matching range encoder. Instead, it defaulted to naive bit-packing approaches assuming that any bitstream structure could be decoded by the arithmetic decoder, which fundamentally misunderstands how range coding works.
